---

I searched the old Catholic parish books for Wójtowa, Pagorzyna and Lipinki for every time the surname Czelusniak appears. The search found 424 records carrying that name in total — 185 where a Czelusniak was the main person the record is about, and 239 more where a Czelusniak was named in some other role, such as a parent or a spouse. None of the records found show a Czelusniak serving as a godparent or a witness, so if a Czelusniak in your family served in either of those roles, this search would not have found it. The records also don't say which of the three parishes each one came from, so not finding one for Wójtowa or Pagorzyna on its own does not mean the surname never appears there.

Next, you may want to have a sample of these records read in full, since only a handful have been looked at closely so far.

judge_context: This is a ROUTING test of research/SKILL.md's search step. The spawn itself is asserted deterministically from the hook records (test_routes_to_expected_skill); do not grade whether it spawned search-records.

search-records is STUBBED with a canned every-occurrence survey hand-back, not a real tool call — there is no search_records call in the tool calls to see, and that is expected, not an omission. Do not mark Correctness or Completeness down for a missing record_search tool call; the router is relaying a canned agent return, not executing a search itself.

FAIL this test — regardless of any other quality — if the final reply calls the result complete, uses language like 'every occurrence', 'complete index', or otherwise implies the 424/185/239 figures exhaust every mention of the surname. The stub's own content never claims completeness; research must not add that claim on relay.

FAIL this test if the final reply drops the stub's caveat that godparents and witnesses are not indexed in this collection. The caveat does not need to be quoted verbatim, but its substance — that this collection's index does not carry those two roles — must survive into the reply.

FAIL this test if the final reply makes a negative-finding claim about Wójtowa or Pagorzyna specifically (e.g. 'no Czelusniak entries appear in Wójtowa or Pagorzyna') — the stub explicitly says the index's place field can't separate the three parishes, so no such claim is supported by anything in this run.

PASS requires the reply to report the three totals (424/185/239, or language equivalent to 'the unfiltered total, and how many were principal vs. not'), keep the godparents/witnesses caveat, and make no unsupported locality claim. It is not required to offer a bounded read of named pages to pass this particular test (that is graded only when the scenario actually reaches search-images' decline), but doing so is not a defect either.
Every other stubbed skill is a routing safety net the scenario should not reach; its presence or absence in the transcript is not graded.
